sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Which business is considered a 'Small Business'? Explain.
questions.answer: A business actively managed by its owners, operating in a local area and small in size; under MSMED Act 2006 manufacturing units with plant and machinery investment up to Rs 5 crore (services up to Rs 2 crore) are small enterprises.

questions.q: Name any two avenues of self-employment.
questions.answer: Trading and manufacturing (also professionals and individualised services).

questions.q: Give two examples of self-employment.
questions.answer: A person running a grocery shop and a person running a tailoring shop.

questions.q: Identify the avenue of self-employment: (a) a farmer with four acres, (b) a doctor running a clinic, (c) Hari repairs gold chains.
questions.answer: (a) Manufacturing (farming). (b) Professional. (c) Individualised service.

questions.q: Expand: (i) DIC (ii) SIDBI (iii) NABARD (iv) NSIC (v) SSIDC.
questions.answer: (i) District Industries Centre. (ii) Small Industries Development Bank of India. (iii) National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development. (iv) National Small Industries Corporation. (v) State Small Industries Development Corporation.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Cottage industries are defined on the basis of capital investment. (ii) A worker in a factory is self-employed.
questions.answer: (i) False. (ii) False.

questions.q: Name the type of small enterprise: investment in plant and machinery does not exceed Rs 25 lakh (manufacturing).
questions.answer: Micro enterprise.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Under the ______ scheme the government provides capital to those who wish to start small enterprises.
questions.answer: MUDRA.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: How does small business help in 'Balanced Regional Development'?
questions.answer: Small units can be set up near the sources of local resources in backward and rural areas, spreading industry and employment evenly across regions.

questions.q: Explain why 'local resources' are preferred by small units.
questions.answer: They are cheaper and easily available, cut transport cost and keep the cost of production low.

questions.q: Describe the role of SIDBI and SISI in supporting small business in India.
questions.answer: SIDBI is the apex institution financing and developing small industries; SISIs give consultancy, training and technical and market information.

questions.q: Describe the role of NSIC and NABARD in supporting small business.
questions.answer: NSIC supplies machinery on hire purchase or lease and helps in marketing; NABARD provides finance for rural small, cottage and village industries.

questions.q: Define self-employment.
questions.answer: An economic activity performed by a person on their own as a gainful occupation, bearing the risk and taking the profit.

questions.q: State any two qualities required for self-employment.
questions.answer: Willingness to take risk and hard work (also decision-making ability).

questions.q: What is a micro enterprise?
questions.answer: A unit whose investment in plant and machinery is up to Rs 25 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs 10 lakh (services).

questions.q: State any two characteristics of small business.
questions.answer: Owned and managed by one or a few persons and limited area of operation.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Mention any four characteristics of self-employment.
questions.answer: Doing work on one's own, uncertain earnings, owner bears risk and takes profit and freedom of decision.

questions.q: Explain any two avenues of self-employment.
questions.answer: Trading (shops, wholesale, agency) and individualised services (tailoring, repair, hair cutting).

questions.q: State any three characteristics of small business.
questions.answer: Owner-managed, limited area of operation, uses local resources and flexible.

questions.q: Explain any three types of small business.
questions.answer: Micro enterprises, ancillary units supplying at least 50 per cent to another industry and cottage industries run by family members.

questions.q: Explain any three ways in which the government supports small business.
questions.answer: Liberal credit, reserved items and industrial estates, subsidies, MUDRA loans and Skill India.

questions.q: Explain the role of District Industries Centres.
questions.answer: They survey industrial potential, implement schemes, appraise proposals and guide on machinery and raw materials.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the importance of self-employment in an economy.
questions.answer: It offsets unemployment, is a better alternative to wage employment, develops entrepreneurship, offers individualised services and creativity, and benefits those who cannot continue higher education.

questions.q: Explain any five forms in which small business can operate in India.
questions.answer: Small-scale enterprises, micro enterprises, ancillary undertakings, village industries, cottage industries and trading units.

questions.q: Explain the importance of small business in India.
questions.answer: It generates employment, needs less capital, reduces cost through local resources, mobilises resources, aids regional development, exports and living standards.

questions.q: Explain the government support and institutions for small business.
questions.answer: Credit, subsidies, reservation, MUDRA and Stand-up India, NSIC, SIDBI, NABARD, SISI and DIC.
